title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells - Nature Biotechnology
gist: DynaVelo is a generative neural-ODE model that learns joint RNA and transcription-factor motif-accessibility dynamics from single-cell multiome data and supports in silico perturbation. Applied to mouse germinal-center B cells, it recovered known trajectories and predicted Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss, which double-heterozygous mouse experiments confirmed by restoring the dark-zone/light-zone ratio.

insights.claim: DynaVelo is a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that jointly learns gene-expression and TF motif-activity dynamics from single-cell multiome data, learning a functional vector field so it can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A perturbable generative model of cell dynamics is the step from descriptive to predictive single-cell AI.
insights.quote: DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories.

insights.claim: Existing velocity tools each miss something: MultiVelo gives no functional vector field so it cannot simulate interventions; Dynamo needs metabolic labeling that many systems cannot provide; scDiffEq uses RNA only and ignores scATAC-derived TF activity.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Defines DynaVelo's competitive niche versus other single-cell dynamics methods.

insights.claim: DynaVelo embeds RNA and chromVAR motif-accessibility matrices with a variational encoder, learns the neural ODE in a 50-dimensional latent space per modality, and is supervised by scVelo velocities for about 400 to 1,000 velocity genes plus an RNA-motif velocity consistency loss.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Architecture details show a fairly small model that other labs can reproduce.
insights.locator: Because solving these ODEs in the original high-dimensional

insights.claim: Training DynaVelo on 5,000 to 20,000 cells typically takes at most 3 hours on a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU with 49 GB of VRAM.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Low compute needs make adoption and replication easy for labs and biotech teams.
insights.locator: Model optimization was performed using the Adam optimizer

insights.claim: No single setting of the prior-regularization weight suits all tasks: a high value (1,000) gives smooth latent times, while a low value (1) gives better in silico perturbation prediction.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Users must tune the model per task, which limits plug-and-play deployment.

insights.claim: Authors advise not to supervise DynaVelo strongly on scVelo velocities unless scVelo already captures the expected trajectories, because velocity estimates are error-prone and domain expertise is needed to judge them.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Garbage-in risk: model quality depends on the upstream velocity estimates.

themes.theme: Latent time and GC B-cell trajectories

insights.claim: On 7,166 wild-type mouse germinal-center B cells, DynaVelo's vector field recovered the bifurcation between centroblast cycling and the centroblast-to-centrocyte transition, plus centrocyte recirculation to the dark zone and exits to prememory B cells and plasmablasts.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Capturing the hard recirculation trajectory is the benchmark showing the model handles complex dynamics.
insights.locator: We first applied DynaVelo to a single-cell multiome dataset

insights.claim: DynaVelo's latent times matched germinal-center dynamics better than scVelo's, which missed the major bifurcation between dark-zone cycling cells and cells moving to the light zone, especially in motif space.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Head-to-head evidence that adding TF motif accessibility improves trajectory inference.

insights.claim: MultiVelo failed on the same data: its velocities ran from centrocyte to centroblast instead of the dominant centroblast-to-centrocyte direction and it labeled plasmablasts as a starting population rather than a germinal-center exit.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A concrete failure mode of the main multiome competitor.

insights.claim: Spi1 and Nfkb1 motif accessibility rises monotonically from centroblast to centrocyte but not during cell-cycle progression, and motif accessibility showed stronger dynamics than RNA expression for these TFs, so the chromatin modality adds information beyond RNA.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Supports the case for multiome rather than RNA-only dynamic models.
insights.quote: Motif accessibility demonstrated stronger dynamics than RNA expression for these TFs

insights.claim: A TF's motif accessibility alone does not reveal its role: Prdm1 is accessible in both prememory B cells and plasmablasts but expressed only in plasmablasts, so RNA expression is needed alongside accessibility.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Single-modality readouts mislead; joint models are needed for TF driver calls.
insights.locator: For the prememory B cell state

insights.claim: DynaVelo flagged Foxo1, Mef2b, Mef2c and Pou2f2 as possible drivers of centroblast cell-cycle progression, since their motif accessibility rises with cycling and falls on transition to centrocytes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Candidate regulators for follow-up in B-cell lymphoma biology.
insights.locator: While key TFs for prememory B cells and plasmablasts

themes.theme: Arid1a and Ctcf mutant germinal centers

insights.claim: In both Arid1a-heterozygous and Ctcf-heterozygous germinal centers, the recirculation of centrocytes back to centroblasts is lost, which likely causes premature exit as prememory B cells instead of repeated rounds of affinity maturation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Links chromatin-regulator loss, which is common in B-cell lymphomas, to a specific loss of affinity maturation.
insights.locator: Heterozygous mutations in Arid1a and Ctcf disrupt

insights.claim: Prememory B cells made up 20.09% of Arid1aHet, 25.45% of CtcfHet and 44.96% of Arid1aHom germinal-center cells versus 5.42% in wild type.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Quantifies the premature-exit phenotype that the model reproduces.
insights.quote: the percentage of prememory B cells in the mutant samples (20.09% in Arid1aHet, 25.45% in CtcfHet and 44.96% in Arid1aHom) is increased compared to WT (5.42%)
insights.locator: Indeed, the percentage of prememory B cells

insights.claim: Ctcf motif accessibility rises significantly in both centroblasts and centrocytes of Arid1aHet cells, suggesting Arid1a and Ctcf act antagonistically in the germinal center; CtcfHet showed a stronger TF-activity phenotype than Arid1aHet.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The antagonism hypothesis underlies the double-mutant rescue strategy.
insights.locator: To identify key TFs disrupted in mutant GCs

insights.claim: Dynamic GRN analysis found that the Spi1-to-Bcl6 upregulation edge present in wild type is lost in both Arid1aHet and CtcfHet cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Identifies a specific regulatory edge broken in mutants.
insights.locator: One key regulatory edge in the GC

insights.claim: Foxo1-to-Cxcr4 upregulation is lost in Arid1aHet centrocytes, a plausible reason they cannot migrate back to the dark zone and instead exit as premature prememory B cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Gives a mechanistic hypothesis for a lymphoma-relevant phenotype.
insights.locator: One critical transcriptional GRN edge in WT GCs

insights.claim: The Bcl6-to-Bcl2 regulatory sign in the centrocyte-to-prememory transition differs in both mutants from wild type, where Bcl6 repression of Bcl2 is relieved after T cell help, suggesting Arid1a and Ctcf act through the Bcl6-Bcl2 axis.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The Bcl6-Bcl2 axis is a known lymphoma target, so this ties the findings to oncology.

themes.theme: In silico rescue prediction and validation

insights.claim: Perturbing Arid1a in silico in wild-type cells predicted reduced centroblast-centrocyte connectivity and strong centrocyte-to-prememory flow, with higher prediction accuracy for motif velocities than for RNA velocities.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Shows forward prediction of loss-of-function effects works better on the chromatin modality.

insights.claim: Perturbing Arid1aHet cells in silico nominated Tox, Bcor, Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as potential rescue targets, with Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 taken forward for testing.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Model-nominated targets for a genetic-interaction screen reduce experimental search space.
insights.locator: As a final application of DynaVelo

insights.claim: Single-cell multiome of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet double-heterozygous germinal centers showed the rapid centrocyte-to-prememory exit partially reversed, matching the in silico Ctcf perturbation; in centrocytes the rescue rates were 38% for RNA expression, 64% for RNA velocity, 51% for motif accessibility and 46% for motif velocity.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Quantified partial rescue, not full, so effects are directional rather than complete.

insights.claim: Heterozygous loss of Bcl6 or Stat3 in Arid1aHet mice restored the elevated dark-zone to light-zone ratio to wild-type levels, confirming two more DynaVelo predictions in newly generated mouse models (54 samples overall).
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Prospective in vivo confirmation of model predictions is the strongest validation in the paper.
insights.quote: The DZ/LZ ratio was restored to WT levels in both compound heterozygous backgrounds
insights.locator: A defining feature of Arid1aHet GCs

insights.claim: All three DynaVelo-nominated rescue targets (Ctcf, Bcl6, Stat3) functionally rescued an in vivo Arid1a-loss phenotype, so in silico perturbation can identify genetic interactions and nominate rescue strategies for loss-of-function disease alleles.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Supports using perturbation-capable single-cell models for target nomination in genetic disease and lymphoma.
insights.quote: These results demonstrate that DynaVelo’s in silico perturbation framework can identify genetic interactions and nominate experimentally tractable rescue strategies for loss-of-function disease alleles.

insights.claim: The authors note that most single-cell genomics is destructive, that velocity estimates are error-prone and computable only for a small gene subset, and that separating causal drivers from confounded ones remains a core challenge.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Frames the structural limits of snapshot-based dynamic inference.

insights.claim: Code is released on GitHub and Zenodo, and processed AnnData objects plus new multiome samples (GEO GSE334370) are public, so results are reproducible.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Open code and data lower the barrier for commercial or academic reuse.

Melnick has had research funding from Janssen, Epizyme and Daiichi Sankyo and consulted for Exo Therapeutics, Treeline Biosciences, AstraZeneca and Epizyme.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Shows which biotech and pharma names are connected to the lymphoma epigenetics group.
